newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T/N rates rise, market seen tight until Wed.
newsitem.headline: Polish T/N rates rise, market seen tight until Wed.

text.p: Polish one-day deposit rates increased throughout the day on Monday as banks searched for cash with only two days left in October's required reserve period, which ends on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Overnight rates began at Friday's levels and gradually rose to close around 20.5 percent, and tomorrow/next were even higher," said Aleksandra Skiba of Bank Zachodni SA.
Dealers said increased demand for cash was likely to keep one-day rates underpinned for the rest of the October account despite some liquidity on the money market last week.
O/N rates closed at 19.50/20.5 percent, down from intraday highs at 21 percent, but above 18.95/19.25 percent at opening.
T/N were at 20.20/21.20 percent against 19.00/19.20 percent at 0745 GMT.
Dealers said the central bank's decision not to stage an open market operation on Monday signalled that the market could be tight over the next few days.
The money market's low liquidity also curbed demand at today's 950 million zloty primary T-bill auction to 867 million zlotys and drove yields higher, dealers said.

The average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill rose 0.01 point to 19.47 percent and the minimum price dipped 0.02 to 83.53. The 26-week paper's yield rose 0.05 to 19.16 percent and the 13-week bill's average yield held flat at 18.55 percent.
The Polish zloty closed a fraction stronger at 1.86/1.81 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's close at 1.82/1.78 percent after an uneventful Monday session.
The zloty was at 2.8215/25 to the dollar, up from 2.8245/52 on Friday, and at 1.8522/35 to the mark, flat from 1.8525/35.
